newsitem.title: USA: Integrated to buy RoTech for $864 million, including debt.
newsitem.headline: Integrated to buy RoTech for $864 million, including debt.

text.p: Integrated Health Services Inc. said Monday it agreed to acquire RoTech Medical Corp. for about $570 million in stock and will also assume about $300 million in debt.
The deal will create one of the nation's largest companies offering home nursing and other home healthcare, inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation services and skilled nursing care.

The combined company will have annual revenues of about $2.3 billion and home health revenues of more than $1 billion. It will operate over 975 home health locations and over 1,500 rehabilitative facilities in 43 states for patients recovering from acute ailments, the companies said.

"This transaction allows us to not only greatly expand our network of home respiratory and home infusion services, it also propels our geographic expansion into rural markets," Robert Elkins, chairman of Integrated, said in a statement.

"The transaction makes a lot of sense," said Morgan Stanley Dean Witter analyst D. Scott Mackesy. "Integrated has a big presence in the home nursing business, but not in respiratory, intravenous therapy or durable medical equipment."
"The (RoTech) acquisition is similar to the Coram acquisition. It brings in the respiratory therapy and intravenous business lines," he said.

The deal came three months after Owings Mills, Md.-based Integrated terminated its merger pact with Coram Healthcare Corp. That deal was valued at $655 million, including debt assumption, when it was announced last October.
Integrated, already the nation's fourth-largest provider of home health care services, paid Coram $21 million in a settlement related to the aborted deal, it said.
Integrated Executive Vice President Marc Levin declined to comment on why the Coram deal fell apart.

RoTech, a diversified provider of home health services based in Orlando, Fla., is the third-largest provider of home respiratory services. Based on its latest quarterly results, the company has annualized revenues of about $440 million. It operates 600 locations in 34 states.
The RoTech deal calls for Integrated to issue 0.5806 shares of common stock for each RoTech common share outstanding. Integrated will also assume about $300 million in RoTech debt.
The merger is expected to close before the end of the year, subject to approval by stockholders, Integrated's senior lenders and regulators, the companies said.
Integrated shares fell $3.25 to $35.69 on the New York Stock Exchange. RoTech climbed $1.125 to $20 on Nasdaq.
Levin noted that the transaction will immediately boost Integrated's per-share earnings but declined to provide details.

According to First Call, analysts' consensus forecast for Integrated's 1998 earnings, the period to be most affected by the deal, is $3.00 a share. That would be up from $2.57 a share expected for 1997, and up from $2.53 a share, or $59.7 million, in 1996 before one-time items.
